units: SI: kg, m, N, s, Pa; axes: +Y is the part's up/nose axis

parts.name: Pebble-1 Crew Pod
parts.description: One penguin, one window, one very brave decision.

parts.name: Huddle-3 Crew Capsule
parts.description: Three penguins sharing body heat and one snack bag.

parts.name: Snowball SC-1 Probe Core
parts.description: No penguin aboard: a little brain that steers by itself. For satellites, probes and test flights nobody has to sit through.

parts.name: Icebox-S Propellant Tank
parts.description: A lunchbox of liquid propellant.

parts.name: Icebox-M Propellant Tank
parts.description: The fridge-sized option.

parts.name: Icebox-L Propellant Tank
parts.description: Walk-in freezer. Mostly propellant, partly ambition.

parts.name: Icebox-XM Wide Propellant Tank
parts.description: Twice as wide as the Icebox line: four times the propellant for its height.

parts.name: Icebox-XL Wide Propellant Tank
parts.description: A whole cold store. Pair it with a big engine, or a mount full of small ones.

parts.name: Walrus LE-215 Lifter Engine
parts.description: Loud, heavy, and happiest at sea level.

parts.name: Albatross VE-60 Vacuum Engine
parts.description: Huge bell, gentle push, glides forever. Sulks in air.

parts.name: Puffling SE-20 Small Engine
parts.description: Small, efficient, and perfect for landers.

parts.name: Narwhal Solid Booster
parts.description: Light it and hold on. There is no off switch.

parts.name: Elephant Seal BE-900 Heavy Engine
parts.description: The wide engine for wide tanks. Shakes the whole glacier.

parts.name: Crack-1 Stack Decoupler
parts.description: Separates stages with a satisfying crack.

parts.name: Crack-2 Wide Stack Decoupler
parts.description: The Crack-1, twice as wide and twice as loud.

parts.name: Calving Radial Decoupler
parts.description: Lets boosters drift off like icebergs.

parts.name: Siphon Feed Line
parts.description: Pipes propellant from the tank it sits on into the tank it points at. Put it on a side tank facing the core: the side tank runs dry first, so you can drop it early.

parts.name: Iceberg Adapter
parts.description: Narrows a wide stack down to the 1.25 m parts (or widens it, flipped). Propellant flows straight through.

parts.name: Rookery Tri-Mount
parts.description: Hangs three 1.25 m engines (or anything else) under a wide stack. Propellant flows through to all three.

parts.name: Toastmaster Heat Shield
parts.description: A thick ablative dish. Goes on the bottom, faces the fire, keeps the penguin cool.

parts.name: Flipper Fin
parts.description: Keeps the pointy end forward, and steers in the air.

parts.name: Featherfall Parachute
parts.description: Opens the sky's softest pillow.

parts.name: Waddle Landing Leg
parts.description: Short, sturdy, and always a little wobbly.

parts.name: Beak Nosecone
parts.description: Sharp enough to part the air, too dull to hurt the air's feelings.

parts.name: Big Beak Nosecone
parts.description: The Beak, for the wide tanks. Same point, four times the shoulders.

parts.name: Spin-Cycle Reaction Wheel
parts.description: A washing machine for attitude.

parts.name: Puffer RV-4 RCS Block
parts.description: Four little monopropellant jets: up, down and both ways round. Mount them in symmetric sets around the CoM and arm them with R. They steer when the wheels aren't enough, and slide the craft sideways for docking.

parts.name: Spritz-80 Radial Mono Tank
parts.description: A ball of monopropellant for the RCS. Every RCS block on the craft drinks from every mono tank, decouplers or not.

parts.name: Spritz-400 Mono Tank
parts.description: A short 1.25 m drum of monopropellant for RCS-heavy work: docking, fine orbit trims, probes.

parts.name: Huddle-Lock Docking Port
parts.description: Two of these meeting face to face, lined up and slow (under 0.8 m/s), lock the craft together. Fuel flows through. U lets go again. Put one on the nose of each craft you want to join.

parts.name: Penguin on EVA
parts.description: A penguin out of the pod: walks (WASD), jumps (Space), climbs back in from anywhere on the hull (F), and on a jetpack's few kilograms of mono flies about (R, then WASD and Shift / Ctrl). It carries a zapper too: hold the left mouse button on whatever is after it.

parts.name: Fishbone Thermometer
parts.description: Reads the temperature wherever it is. Stick it on, press SCIENCE (O) when somewhere new, and bring the reading home.

parts.name: Puffball Barometer
parts.description: Measures the air pressure: on the ground, in the air, and (to make sure) the nothing of low orbit.

parts.name: Snowflake Lab
parts.description: A stack-mounted lab that grows and studies snowflakes wherever it goes. Heavy, but the research is worth it.

parts.name: Gannet Wing
parts.description: A proper wing: lifts once you're moving, and its aileron flap rolls you. Put one on each side, a little behind the centre of mass.

parts.name: Skua J-90 Jet Engine
parts.description: Breathes the air it flies through: very little fuel for its push, but none at all in space, and nothing left past about 520 m/s. Thicker air, more thrust.

parts.name: Waddle-Wheel Landing Gear
parts.description: A sprung wheel for runways. It rolls along the craft's nose and grips sideways; B brakes. Fit them on the belly near the centre of mass.

parts.name: Waddle-Wheel Nose Gear
parts.description: The steering wheel: fit one under the nose, ahead of the centre of mass. It turns with the yaw keys while you roll.

parts.name: Krill-Cell Battery Pack
parts.description: Stores 2000 kJ of electricity for the reaction wheels and probe cores. Pods carry a little of their own.

parts.name: Sunfin Solar Panel
parts.description: 1.5 kW facing the sun at Floe's distance from Austra; more nearer it, less further out, none in a planet's shadow. Its face looks out from the hull.

parts.name: Squawk Antenna
parts.description: Sends experiment results home from wherever you are (O, then Send): half a result's worth, for 20 kJ of electricity per research point.

parts.name: Earhole Signal Scanner
parts.description: A little dish tuned to the strange hum. With the power on it hears a signal source in sight of it up to 3,000 km away and gives its distance and heading.

parts.name: Tern Laser Turret
parts.description: A laser on a swivel: 60 hp a second to whatever it meets first, out to 1.5 km, for 15 kW while it fires. Fire it by hand (hold the left mouse button on what you want gone), or from a script: ship.fire_at(thing) (guard.py keeps the ground round the ship clear).

parts.name: Waddle Ladder
parts.description: Three metres of rungs. A penguin on EVA who can reach it can climb it to the hatch: fit one on a tall rocket so the crew can get back aboard from the ground.

parts.name: PASA Flag
parts.description: Planted by a penguin on EVA (G): it stays where it stands, for good.

parts.name: Gizzard Ore Bin
parts.description: Holds 1500 kg of ore dug by a drill until a refinery turns it into propellant. Starts empty.

parts.name: Pecker Ore Drill
parts.description: Digs ore (0.25 kg/s where it's richest, for 0.75 kW) while the craft rests on the ground with the drill within 2 m of it: fit it low on a lander. C switches mining on and off (or put it in an action group).

parts.name: Sifter Refinery
parts.description: Turns 0.5 kg/s of ore into 0.4 kg/s of liquid propellant for 2 kW, filling every propellant tank aboard. Works landed or in orbit.

parts.name: Stillwater Drive
parts.description: Alien. It pulls every atom of the ship alike, so nobody aboard feels a thing: 100 g between the stars (where it can push a ship toward light speed), up to 1 g inside a star's heliopause and never past 1% of light speed there. Needs 40 MW: a Hearth Core. Shift/Ctrl set its throttle in flight.

parts.name: Hearth Core
parts.description: Alien. A steady 45 MW from something no penguin understands yet, in the dark or the light, with a 20 MJ buffer.

parts.name: Burrow Hab Module
parts.description: A room with six windows for two penguins on a long trip. Climb inside (I) and float, or stand on the aft wall while the engines push: thrust is weight in here.

parts.name: Rookery Wide Hab
parts.description: Five metres across: a whole colony's common room, twelve windows round the middle. It narrows at both ends to fit the 1.25 m stack.

parts.name: Iceframe Crew Spine
parts.description: Four metres of open truss round a crawl tube: puts distance between the crew and the engines (or the reactor) and still lets a penguin through.

parts.name: Iceframe Truss
parts.description: Open girders, nothing inside: light, and anything can hang off its sides.

parts.name: Six-Way Huddle Junction
parts.description: A pressurised box with a hatch on every face: build sideways. Habs, spines and tanks fit any of its six nodes, and penguins pass between them through the box.

parts.name: Carousel Spin Ring
parts.description: A 32 m wheel for eight penguins round a 1.25 m hub, four spokes out to a deck 16 m from the axis. Spun at 7.5 rpm (J, with SAS on) the deck weighs a penguin about as much as Floe does; nearer the hub, less. Its motors take a minute to spin a light ship up, longer a heavy one.

parts.name: Icebox Stretch Tank
parts.description: Any size you like: resize it in the hangar from a stubby 0.6 m to an 8 m long, 5 m wide cold store. Propellant and mass go with its volume.

parts.name: Floe-Block Hull
parts.description: A square-sided hull section, any width, depth and length: build boxy ships. A node on every face, and anything can stick to its sides.

parts.name: Square Icebox Tank
parts.description: A propellant tank with flat sides, for hulls that aren't round. Resizes on all three sides.

parts.name: Prow Wedge
parts.description: Square at the bottom, a blade at the top: a ship's prow, a tail, a fairing for a boxy hull. Resizes on all three sides.

parts.name: Igloo Box Hab
parts.description: A square room for four with its own reaction wheels, resizable: stretch it into a long corridor or a wide hall. Walk about inside (Enter); its floor is whichever wall what you feel presses you to.

parts.name: Glasswing Hull
parts.description: Alien. Copied from the Hearth's own casing: a third the weight of a Floe-Block, and it shrugs off 4000 K, so a ship of it comes home through the air without a heat shield.

parts.name: Glasswing Prow
parts.description: Alien. The Glasswing hull as a blade-edged prow: light, and good to 4000 K on the way back down.

parts.name: Hearth Torch
parts.description: Alien, half understood: a white-hot jet of ordinary propellant at fifteen times a rocket's exhaust speed, 800 kN of it. The jet carries some 20 GW; the 40 MW it draws (a Hearth Core) only holds the fire, and nobody at PASA knows where the rest comes from. Short of those 40 MW it gives what the power pays for. Real thrust: felt aboard as weight.

parts.name: Jaeger Hull
parts.description: The Jaegers' own: a lens of dark metal with its pilot inside. Break it and the rest of the ship falls.

parts.name: Jaeger Lift Drive
parts.description: It pushes the ship whichever way the pilot likes, and nothing comes out of it.

parts.name: Jaeger Lance
parts.description: The Jaegers' laser: 10 hp a second out to 900 m.
